## Numbered, cross-referenceable equations

Write display math in LaTeX and label it for cross-reference:

$$
y = X\beta + \varepsilon, \qquad \varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 I).
$$ {#eq-example}

Refer back to it as @eq-example.

## Citations

umbrella (additive, deduplicated).

## Executable figures (lightweight, CI-safe)

Lightweight figures execute at build time using numpy/matplotlib only — never
JAX, native FFI, or GPU (SPEC §6.4):

```{python}
#| label: fig-example
#| fig-cap: "Replace with a figure that illustrates a real idea."
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3))
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.title("placeholder — replace me")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

For anything heavy, HPC-only, or not reproducible in CI, **freeze** it: compute
offline, commit the artifact under `_resources/generated/`, and embed it as a
static image instead of executing here.

## Cross-library references

Link a *curated* anchor in another library with the federation shortcode (shown
escaped; remove one brace layer to use it):
`{{{< xref nitrix:fellner-schall "the Fellner–Schall chapter" >}}}`.
Register the target in `xref/namespaces.yml` first — only deliberately exposed
anchors are cross-referenceable.
